title: AWS Fargate Task Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.77 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.77 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:metric` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:metric" Namespace="AWS/ECS" MetricName="CPUUtilization"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.77_aws_fargate_task_health_77"
| sort -_time
description: Fargate tasks are the unit of scale; tracking stopped tasks and resource limits surfaces platform issues before services miss SLAs.
value: Detecting aws fargate task health early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable CloudWatch Container Insights for ECS on Fargate and pull metrics via `Splunk_TA_aws` CloudWatch metric input. Ship task and service logs to Splunk (FireLens, Lambda, or direct subscription) and run a companion search on `sourcetype=aws:cloudwatchlogs` for `Task stopped` / error patterns. Map dimensions `ClusterName`, `ServiceName`, `TaskId`. Alert on sustained high CPU/memory, task stop reasons, and log error bursts.
visualization: Time chart (CPU/memory by service), Table (stopped tasks with reason), Single value (running task count).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` max(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as peak
  from datamodel=Performance.All_Performance
  by Performance.object Performance.host span=1h
| where isnotnull(peak)
| sort - peak
dataModelAcceleration: Performance: enable if `aws:cloudwatch` (or your metric store) is mapped to CIM Performance, or use `mstats` on the same CloudWatch metrics. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.

references.title: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services

knownFalsePositives: Planned deploys, game-day tests, and vendor maintenance that you expect to move CPU, error, or lag metrics; compare with the change window.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:metric`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable CloudWatch Container Insights for ECS on Fargate and pull metrics via `Splunk_TA_aws` CloudWatch metric input. Ship task and service logs to Splunk (FireLens, Lambda, or direct subscription) and run a companion search on `sourcetype=aws:cloudwatchlogs` for `Task stopped` / error patterns. Map dimensions `ClusterName`, `ServiceName`, `TaskId`. Alert on sustained high CPU/memory, task stop reasons, and log error bursts.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:metric" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:metric" Namespace="AWS/ECS" MetricName="CPUUtilization"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.77_aws_fargate_task_health_77"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:metric` in `index=cloud` to detect aws fargate task health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_77_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Time chart (CPU/memory by service), Table (stopped tasks with reason), Single value (running task count)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of aws fargate task health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
